case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Sheo Lal and Others
facts: The challenge in these appeals is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Allahabad High Court directing acquittal of the respondents.
In the evening of 20.3.1979 at about 6.00 pm Km. Sharmi (PW 4) was going to attend the call of nature.
Sheo Lal accompanied by Suresh and Surendra came to the house of Krishanapal, deceased.
The F.I.R. of the incident was lodged by Vijaypal (P.W.3).
Chandrapal (P.W.2) was sent from the police station to the Primary Health Center, Bidhnoo for medical examination of his injuries.
After completion of investigation charge sheet was filed.
As the accused persons pleaded innocence trial was held.
issues: The motive suggested is clearly unacceptable as the parties are inter-se related and it is improbable that the accused persons will tried to molest their cousin (PW 4) in the manner as alleged by the prosecution.
What appears to have weighed with the High Court to doubt versity of prosecution version is the introduction of a witness i.e. Munni Devi regarding the motive.
Merely because the colour of the injury was not noted and the doctor has written that the injury was fresh, that is no ground to discard his evidence.
petitioner_arguments: The conclusions of the High Court are absolutely unsustainable.
What appears to have weighed with the High Court to doubt versity of prosecution version is the introduction of a witness i.e. Munni Devi regarding the motive.
There were contradictory observations and no reason has been indicated to discard the version of the injured eye witnesses.
respondent_arguments: The judgment of the High Court at one place noticed that it is improbable that the accused person who was cousin of PW 4 tried to molest her.
In the same breath the High Court in another place has held that the accused persons to molest PW 4 at a particular moment took her to the Arhar field and this was done with her prior consent.
court_reasoning: The doctor's evidence was discarded on the ground that his testimony was of poor quality and does not inspire confidence.
The High Court has also attached unnecessary importance to the fact that one witness stated that the assault continued for 8 to 10 minutes while another said it was around three minutes.
The judgment is full of contradictions.
holding: The judgment of the trial court is restored.
The respondents shall surrender to custody forthwith to serve the remainder of sentence.
cases_cited: In Nathuni Yadav v. State of Bihar
State of Uttar Pradesh v Sheo Lal
The position was reiterated in Bharosi v. State of M
and S. Sudershan Reddy v. State of A
